app.setup.title_default.why: Follows the Apple System Settings pattern ('Wi-Fi Desativado'): state, past participle. Does not repeat the button below.

app.setup.title_failed.why: Hedged, not a verdict — reads clearly apart from the plain 'Extensão desativada'.

app.setup.detail_default.s: Depois de ativada, nenhum site protegido consegue mais desviar o seu toque.
app.setup.detail_default.back: Once activated, no protected site can divert your touch/click anymore.
app.setup.detail_default.why: 'Toque' covers both a tap and a click, since the app runs on iPhone, iPad and Mac alike.

app.setup.detail_failed.s: O Safari não respondeu dessa vez. Se você ativar a extensão lá, o app percebe sozinho.
app.setup.detail_failed.back: Safari didn't respond this time. If you turn the extension on there, the app notices on its own.
app.setup.detail_failed.why: No error code, no jargon; the second clause is the reassurance the brief asks for.

app.setup.open_button.why: Names the one action (opens Safari's Extensions pane) without tying it to either screen's framing, so it works on both.

app.welcome.heading.why: The one place allowed a warmer register; app name kept untranslated as a proper noun.

app.welcome.feature.invisible_layers.tit.why: Plain concrete noun phrase naming the trick, no marketing language.

app.welcome.feature.invisible_layers.det.s: Uma camada invisível cobre a página e desvia o seu toque.
app.welcome.feature.invisible_layers.det.back: An invisible layer covers the page and diverts your tap.
app.welcome.feature.invisible_layers.det.why: Describes what the person would see, not the mechanism.

app.welcome.feature.swapped_links.title.why: Two-word noun phrase matching the sibling rows' style.

app.welcome.feature.swapped_links.detail.s: Alguns sites trocam o destino do link bem na hora do toque.
app.welcome.feature.swapped_links.detail.back: Some sites swap the link's destination right at the moment of the tap.
app.welcome.feature.swapped_links.detail.why: Plain description of the experience: the link changes exactly as the press lands.

app.welcome.feature.uninvited_windows.ti.why: Names the trick plainly, matching the icon (macwindow).

app.welcome.feature.uninvited_windows.de.s: Com a proteção ativa, uma aba nova só abre onde você realmente tocou.
app.welcome.feature.uninvited_windows.de.back: With protection active, a new tab only opens where you actually tapped.
app.welcome.feature.uninvited_windows.de.why: Framed as the promise the brief asks for, not a description of the trick.

app.welcome.feature.every_destination.ti.why: Names the app's own rule-list feature: it tracks everything, not just what it stops.

app.welcome.feature.every_destination.de.s: Você revisa cada destino e decide: aqui ou em todos os sites.
app.welcome.feature.every_destination.de.back: You review each destination and decide: here or on every site.
app.welcome.feature.every_destination.de.why: Uses 'aqui'/'em todos os sites', the same scope words used everywhere else in the app.

app.welcome.feature.one_site_at_a_time.t.why: Names the per-site activation model plainly, contrasting with automatic/everywhere mode elsewhere.

app.welcome.feature.one_site_at_a_time.d.s: Toque no botão do Undirect, na barra do Safari, para proteger o site atual.
app.welcome.feature.one_site_at_a_time.d.back: Tap the Undirect button, in the Safari toolbar, to protect the current site.
app.welcome.feature.one_site_at_a_time.d.why: Names the exact mechanism (the toolbar button) rather than a vague 'turn it on'.

app.nav.guarded_sites.why: Works identically as a sidebar row and a navigation title, no wrapping in a narrow column.

app.nav.settings.why: Apple's own Brazilian Portuguese term for the Settings app/section — wins over any synonym.

app.nav.app_title.why: Proper noun, left untranslated like any other app's own name.

app.rules.grouping.everywhere.why: Contrasts cleanly with 'Por site' below; 'geral' is reused for the 'everywhere' scope throughout the app.

app.rules.grouping.by_site.why: Clear opposite of 'Geral' when the two sit side by side in the sidebar.

app.rules.empty_no_app.title.why: A wiring/first-contact state, not 'no content' — distinct from app.rules.empty_no_rules.title.

app.rules.empty_no_app.detail.s: Abra uma página no Safari e a lista aparece sozinha.
app.rules.empty_no_app.detail.back: Open a page in Safari and the list appears on its own.
app.rules.empty_no_app.detail.why: States the simple fix without implying any setting needs changing.

app.rules.empty_no_rules.title.why: Contrasts with 'Sem dados da extensão' — this is a genuinely empty list, not a missing connection.

app.rules.empty_no_rules.detail.s: Uma regra só aparece depois que você decide algo sobre um destino.
app.rules.empty_no_rules.detail.back: A rule only appears after you decide something about a destination.
app.rules.empty_no_rules.detail.why: Explains that seeing a destination isn't enough — a rule needs an actual decision.

app.rules.footer.lifetime_count.why: Kept the %lld ICU placeholder as-is; SwiftUI/String Catalog resolves the pt-BR plural form for it.

app.rules.row.state_blocked.why: One word, reused across the app for the 'block' concept; pairs opposite 'Permitido'.

app.rules.row.action_allow.why: Infinitive as an imperative menu action, distinct from the adjective 'Permitido' used for the current state.

app.rules.row.help_tooltip.why: Short enough for a macOS .help tooltip while naming exactly what the control does.

app.rules.row.use_default.why: Names clearing the explicit rule so the destination falls back to the app's default policy.

app.watched.empty.title.why: States plainly that the guarded-sites list is empty so far.

app.watched.empty.detail.s: Toque no botão do Undirect, na barra do Safari, para proteger um site.
app.watched.empty.detail.back: Tap the Undirect button, in the Safari toolbar, to protect a site.
app.watched.empty.detail.why: Same mechanism wording as the welcome sheet's one_site_at_a_time row, for consistency.

app.watched.footer.s: Sites só entram nesta lista pelo botão do Undirect, no Safari.
app.watched.footer.back: Sites only enter this list through the Undirect button, in Safari.
app.watched.footer.why: Reminds the person this screen can only remove entries, never add them.

app.watched.row.guarded_badge.why: Read-only status word on iOS, where there is no Stop button.

app.watched.row.stop_button.why: Short imperative verb for a small trailing row button on Mac.

app.watched.row.stop_tooltip.back: Turns off protection for this site
app.watched.row.stop_tooltip.why: Describes exactly what the button under the pointer does.

app.settings.guard_toggle.why: The noun form of 'guard', used consistently as the master switch's label throughout the app.

app.settings.state_on.why: Generic on/off word, reused for more than one setting on this screen — kept gender-neutral by default.

app.settings.state_off.why: Clear opposite of 'Ativado', same generic use.

app.settings.mode_heading.why: Introduces the watched-sites-vs-everywhere choice as a heading, matching the extension's own popup wording.

app.settings.mode_watched.why: Describes the default, more conservative mode from the person's own point of view.

app.settings.mode_everywhere.why: Names automatic, always-on mode in two words.

app.settings.banner_toggle.why: Names the on-page banner, distinct from the popup's own record of an attempt.

app.settings.policy_heading.s: Política padrão para destinos sem regra
app.settings.policy_heading.back: Default policy for destinations without a rule
app.settings.policy_heading.why: Spells out the concept in full since this is the last, easy-to-miss section of Settings.

app.settings.policy_block.why: Short imperative picker option; unrated destinations are stopped by default.

app.settings.policy_allow.why: Opposite of 'Bloquear', unrated destinations let through by default.

ext.meta.name.why: Proper noun, same as app.nav.app_title — left untranslated.

ext.meta.description.s: Impede que páginas usem seu clique para abrir ou redirecionar para outro lugar.
ext.meta.description.back: Stops pages from using your click to open or redirect somewhere else.
ext.meta.description.why: One plain sentence for someone who has never used the extension, slightly more explanatory than in-app copy.

ext.meta.app_title.why: Fallback display name for the product itself when no site name is available.

ext.toolbar.tooltip_on.why: States the current tab's guard state as the icon's accessible name.

ext.toolbar.tooltip_off.why: Two short sentences instead of a dash, since Portuguese doesn't carry this kind of clause on a dash; doubles as the call to action.

ext.toolbar.tooltip_no_site.why: Explains briefly that this tab has no actual website.

ext.popup.no_site_title.why: Headline for the empty state on a blank tab or the Start Page.

ext.popup.no_site_body.s: Abra um site e toque aqui para protegê-lo.
ext.popup.no_site_body.back: Open a site and tap here to protect it.
ext.popup.no_site_body.why: 'Aqui' keeps the brief's note: it refers to the toolbar button the popup hangs off of, not a place.

ext.popup.watch_switch_label.why: Screen-reader-only label naming exactly what the switch controls, since the visible row only shows the site name.

ext.popup.watch_unknown.why: Brief reason the per-site switch is disabled.

ext.popup.watch_everywhere_mode.s: Já ativa em todos os sites, nos Ajustes
ext.popup.watch_everywhere_mode.back: Already active on every site, in Settings
ext.popup.watch_everywhere_mode.why: Explains the switch is redundant because the 'every site' mode is already on elsewhere.

ext.popup.watch_master_off.why: Explains the master switch, not this particular site, is why the row is disabled.

ext.popup.watch_on.back: Active. Turning it off reloads the page.
ext.popup.watch_on.why: Confirms the state and warns about the reload in one short line, split as two sentences instead of a dash.

ext.popup.watch_off.back: Inactive. Turning it on reloads the page.
ext.popup.watch_off.why: Direct counterpart to watch_on, same sentence shape.

ext.popup.page_heading.why: Heads the section listing what the current tab specifically tried to reach.

ext.popup.page_off.s: Nada rastreado aqui. A proteção está desligada.
ext.popup.page_off.back: Nothing tracked here. Protection is off.
ext.popup.page_off.why: Dead key as of 2026-09-22 per the brief; written speculatively to match the voice of the other page-section states.

ext.popup.page_quiet.s: Nada tentou sair desta página até agora.
ext.popup.page_quiet.back: Nothing has tried to leave this page so far.
ext.popup.page_quiet.why: States plainly that no attempt has happened on this tab yet.

ext.popup.page_empty.why: Dead key per the brief; treated as a near-synonym of page_quiet rather than inventing a new meaning.

ext.popup.stopped_one.why: Chrome/WebExtension-style $COUNT$ placeholder kept verbatim; singular form of the trailing badge.

ext.popup.seen_one.why: Broader than 'stopped' — every recorded attempt, blocked or allowed, singular case.

ext.popup.tries_one.why: Terse inline fragment meant to sit among other short tags in one detail line.

ext.popup.recipe_heading.why: One-word lead-in fragment, concatenated in code as 'Correção: <fix name>'.

ext.state.blocked.why: Same word as app.rules.row.state_blocked, reused across menu options, row chips and row labels; combines with a scope word after it.

ext.state.removed.why: Feminine to agree with 'armadilha' (trap), the thing this label actually describes, for the one row kind that has no destination to rule on.

ext.scope.here.why: Composes after a verdict word: 'Bloqueado' + 'neste site' -> 'Bloqueado neste site'.

ext.scope.everywhere.why: Composes as 'Bloqueado em geral'; kept to two words rather than one because Portuguese has no single-word equivalent of 'everywhere' that reads naturally after a verdict — reuses the 'geral' term from app.rules.grouping.everywhere.

ext.scope.default.why: Composes as 'Bloqueado por padrão', matching the 'default policy' vocabulary term.

ext.action.allow_here.why: Scoped-to-this-site option in the verdict menu.

ext.action.allow_everywhere.why: Everywhere-scoped counterpart, reusing 'geral' for consistency with ext.scope.everywhere.

ext.action.block_here.why: Scoped-to-this-site option in the verdict menu.

ext.popup.policy_heading.s: Política padrão para destinos sem regra
ext.popup.policy_heading.back: Default policy for destinations without a rule
ext.popup.policy_heading.why: Same concept and wording as app.settings.policy_heading, separate translation unit but reads the same to the user.

ext.policy.allow.why: Radio option, short imperative, opposite of 'Bloquear'.

ext.popup.bridge_warning.s: A política de segurança desta página bloqueia parte da proteção aqui.
ext.popup.bridge_warning.back: This page's own security policy blocks part of the protection here.
ext.popup.bridge_warning.why: Frames it as a limitation of this one page, not a bug or a setting to fix, as the brief asks.

ext.kind.click_catcher.why: Terse noun phrase naming an invisible clickable element placed over the page.

ext.kind.overlay.why: Broader than the click-catcher tag: any see-through element over the page, not specifically something clickable.

ext.kind.synthetic_click.why: Names a click the page's own script dispatched, not a real press.

ext.kind.window_open.why: Names a window the page opened through its own script.

ext.kind.form_submit.why: Names the hidden-form-submission trick used to open a new tab.

ext.kind.back_hijack.why: Names a navigation fired right after the person's own back gesture.

ext.kind.redirect.why: Names the core same-tab-redirect trick that hijacks a press aimed elsewhere.

ext.kind.pop_tab.why: Names a new tab opened behind the person's own press, tab-under style.

ext.kind.network_rule.why: Names a destination stopped at the network request itself, the earliest kind of block.

ext.reason.way_back.s: O link volta para o site de origem.
ext.reason.way_back.back: The link leads back to the site of origin.
ext.reason.way_back.why: Explains the redirect was allowed because its own address carried a path back.

ext.reason.sized.s: A janela pediu um tamanho específico.
ext.reason.sized.back: The window asked for a specific size.
ext.reason.sized.why: Explains the window was allowed because it opened at a deliberate size, not as a bare tab.

ext.reason.took_press.why: As terse as the ~15-25 char budget allows, naming the core hijack pattern.

ext.reason.default_allow.why: Explains the destination went through only because no rule blocked it.

ext.reason.own_code.back: Opened by the site's own code.
ext.reason.own_code.why: Explains the window was allowed because the site itself, not a third party, asked for it.

ext.popup.rules_link.why: One word reused as the nav row, the Rules screen's own header, and the back-button's accessible label.

ext.popup.back_link.why: Conventional one-word back-button label; the chevron already shows the direction.

ext.rules.everywhere_heading.why: Reuses 'geral' from the everywhere-scope vocabulary for consistency.

ext.rules.empty.why: Terse single-row placeholder for an empty section.

ext.action.allow.why: Simpler context than allow_here/allow_everywhere since scope is fixed by the section.

ext.action.clear.why: Same phrasing and action as app.rules.row.use_default, for a user moving between the app and the popup.

ext.popup.settings_heading.why: Same Apple term as app.nav.settings, reused as the nav row and that screen's own header title.

ext.settings.guard_label.why: Same term as app.settings.guard_toggle, used both as the visible row label and the sr-only label on the switch.

ext.settings.guard_on.why: Feminine to agree with 'Proteção', specific to the guard switch's own state name.

ext.settings.mode_heading.why: Same wording as app.settings.mode_heading for consistency between the app and the popup.

ext.action.report.why: Names opening a pre-filled issue report; nothing is sent automatically until the person submits it.
